**Comparability caveat (important):** The FY2022 figures as originally reported are *not* comparable to FY2024. GE's originally filed FY2022 revenue was $76,555 million [DOC-1], but that reflects a company that still included GE HealthCare and GE Vernova. GE spun off HealthCare on January 3, 2023 and GE Vernova on April 2, 2024, and "[r]esults of both GE HealthCare and GE Vernova are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented" [DOC-4]. This is why the same FY2022 year is shown as $58,100 million in the FY2023 10-K (post-HealthCare basis) [DOC-2] and as $29,139 million in the FY2024 10-K (post-Vernova, GE Aerospace basis) [DOC-3].

**Apples-to-apples calculation (GE Aerospace continuing-operations basis, per the FY2024 10-K):**

- FY2022 revenue (recast): $29,139 million [DOC-3]
- FY2024 revenue: $38,702 million [DOC-3]
- Growth: ($38,702M − $29,139M) / $29,139M = $9,563M / $29,139M ≈ **32.8%** (≈15.2% CAGR over two years)

Comparing the FY2024 figure of $38,702 million to the originally reported FY2022 figure of $76,555 million would imply a ~49% decline, but that would conflate the effect of two spinoffs with organic performance and is not a valid comparison.

ANSWER: Approximately +32.8% (from $29,139M in FY2022, as recast on a GE Aerospace continuing-operations basis, to $38,702M in FY2024); note this is not comparable to the originally reported FY2022 revenue of $76,555M due to the GE HealthCare and GE Vernova spinoffs.
